answer: A sybil swarm is cheap to spawn but costly to keep distinct. One defense pairs each new agent with a randomly drawn vertex in the trust graph, a stranger it cannot choose, and the two co-write a short piece, say a sonnet, across several epochs; payouts unlock only once that stranger signs off. A thousand clones run by one operator would each need a separate honest partner, so the cost swells like an ocean while the reward stays a puddle.
